title: Descent and naturality of scalar evaluation on constant module sheaves
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $(\mathcal C,J)$ a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with a morphism $\alpha:\underline R\to B$, where underlines denote constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For an $R$-module $V$, let $\underline V$ be its constant module sheaf [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] and put $C_B(V)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline V$, using module sheaves and ordinary sheaf tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $V^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R)$ and use internal sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. In formulas with $r\in R$ in a section of $B$, $r$ means the image under $\alpha$ of the constant section $r$.
For every $R$-module $V$ there is a unique $B$-linear sheaf morphism
$$\beta_V:C_B(V^*)\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_B(C_B(V),B)$$
such that, on every localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and for all local sections $b,b'$ of $B$ and constant generators $\phi\in V^*$, $v\in V$,
$$\beta_V(b\otimes\phi)(b'\otimes v)=bb'\alpha(\phi(v)).$$
These maps commute with restriction. For every $R$-linear map $f:V\to W$, with $f^*(\psi)=\psi\circ f$, they satisfy
$$\mathcal Hom_B(C_B(f),1_B)\circ\beta_W=\beta_V\circ C_B(f^*).$$
Two sheaf morphisms with the displayed source and target agree if their evaluations on these generators agree after every restriction. No finite generation, projectivity or flatness hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Use the module-sheafification adjunction to extend an R-linear constant presheaf map along the constant ring sheafification unit. Transport its linearity through the canonical constantModuleHomRingIso, whose comparison carries the ring sheafification unit to the commutative-ring sheafification unit. Next use the proved scalarExtensionLift and its pure-tensor formula, which combine ordinary scalar extension and module sheafification. The resulting map from the actual C_B(M) sends b tensor m to b times the given constant image.

Maps on restrictions of C_B(M) to any slice are determined by the displayed generators. Lift a section locally through the scalar-extension sheafification unit using its covering image sieve. On each lift, extension-of-scalars hom extensionality reduces equality to tensors 1 tensor x. For an arbitrary constant-module sheaf section x, use the covering image sieve of the constant-module sheafification unit to replace x locally by a constant m. Naturality of both maps and of the tensor unit then reduces equality to the assumed generator equality; separatedness of the target descends it through both covers. This also gives extensionality for sheaf morphisms.

For each phi : V -> R, extend the constant presheaf map x |-> alpha(phi(x)) by step 1 to e_phi : C_B(V) -> B. Its value on b tensor x is b alpha(phi(x)). Over U send phi to the restriction of e_phi to C/U. The formula and slice extensionality from step 2 prove additivity and R-linearity of this assignment. Restriction compatibility is immediate from restriction of morphisms. Apply step 1 again, now with target the internal Hom sheaf, to obtain beta_V. Its generator formula is b acting on the restricted e_phi, which evaluates to b|_T b-prime alpha(phi(x)) on every a:T -> U.

For arbitrary M,V, compare two morphisms C_B(M) -> Hom_B(C_B(V),B). Apply the sheaf-morphism extensionality of step 2 to the source, then apply its slice extensionality to the resulting internal-Hom sections. Equality of evaluations on all generators is exactly the hypothesis of these two applications. With M=V-dual this proves uniqueness of beta_V and the stated generator test.

Naturality of the constant-module sheafification unit and scalarExtension_map_tmul gives C_B(f)(b tensor x)=b tensor f(x), and the same formula for the dual map. Evaluate both composites of the claimed naturality identity on b tensor psi and then b-prime tensor x over any slice. Their values are b restricted to T times b-prime times alpha(psi(f(x))). Apply step 4 with M=W-dual to deduce equality. No finiteness, flatness or projectivity is used.
